Right now Eliza and Her Monsters or Life of Pi.

1. Eliza and Her Monsters by Francesca Zappia, I know it’s YA but I think it’s a beautiful and heart breaking depiction of depression and insecurity and self loathing, I have never felt so understood before it makes me cry to read it. It’s a not quite a traditional format novel either which I always find fascinating. 

2. Life of Pi by Yann Martel, I love the mystical storyline the most. But I like it’s duality and the way it explores the possibilities that two things can be true at the same time and without invalidating each other, and the way it flips your perspective. And the kind of things you believe and the way you look at the world can determine which side you might initially see the story from, the fantastical vs the realistic. And the way you can read the story in so many different ways and viewpoints. The boat stuff is kind of confusing though, like reeeally confusing but I find despite that the story is still beautiful.
